name: AdminEase
author: PrecisionWP

sections.description:
AdminEase is an all-in-one WordPress admin toolkit that helps you manage updates, strengthen security, improve performance and streamline site maintenance without touching code. AdminEase makes everyday site management faster, safer, and easier from a clean, user friendly dashboard.

Is your WordPress admin slow? AdminEase fixes the most common causes and locks down security without touching code.

  • Fixes the slowdowns: Tackles low memory limits, database bloat, and WP-Cron overload, the most common causes of a sluggish admin.
  • Locks down security: Harden your site against common attacks with a click, nothing to configure.
  • One dashboard, 60+ settings: Toggle features on or off anytime, with nothing to break if you change your mind.

Key Benefits

  • No Coding Required: User-friendly interface for all skill levels
  • Enhanced Security: Protect your site from common vulnerabilities
  • Better Performance: Optimize WordPress for speed and efficiency
  • Complete Control: Toggle features on/off anytime without risk
  • Time Saver: Manage dozens of settings from one dashboard

Features

Updates and Notifications

  • Auto Update Core: Enable/disable automatic WordPress core updates.
  • Auto Update Plugins: Enable/disable automatic plugin updates.
  • Auto Update Themes: Enable/disable automatic theme updates.
  • Auto Update Translations: Enable/disable automatic translation updates.
  • Update Notification Emails: Receive emails when core, themes, or plugins are auto-updated.
  • New User Admin Notification Email: Notify admin on a new user registration.
  • User Password Change Admin Notification Email: Notify admin when a user changes their password.
  • Comment Admin Notification Email: Notify admin on new comments.
  • Send Email Through SMTP: Send your site’s email through a real mailbox instead of the web server, so password resets, order confirmations, and contact form messages reach the inbox instead of spam. Includes a test button that reports exactly what your mail server said.
  • Disable Admin Notices: Hide admin notices from plugins and themes.
  • Disable recovery mode email notification: Prevent WordPress from sending recovery mode emails.
  • Customize recovery mode recipient email: Set a custom email address to receive recovery mode notifications.

Security

  • Disable File Edit: Prevent editing theme/plugin files from the admin panel.
  • Disable File Mods: Prevent all file modifications in WordPress, including installing, updating, and deleting plugins and themes.
  • Disable XML-RPC: Block XML-RPC access to reduce attack surface, with an IP allowlist in AdminEase Pro.
  • Disable REST API: Block REST API access, with an IP allowlist in AdminEase Pro, plus the option to allow all HTTP requests to wordpress.org, including plugin/theme updates, version checks, and other API communications.
  • Disable Embeds: Stop automatic embedding of external content.
  • Hide WordPress Version: Remove version info from source code and feeds.
  • Password Protect Site: Protect your entire website with a password, featuring customizable themes, role-based bypasses, IP whitelisting, device remembering, and auto-disable scheduling.
  • Block Access to .htaccess/.htpasswd: Protect sensitive server files.
  • Disable Pingbacks: Prevent XML-RPC pingback abuse.
  • Block Author Scans: Prevent username enumeration.
  • Block Directory Browsing: Stop public directory listing.
  • Disable Script Concatenation (Admin): Prevent certain DoS attacks in admin.
  • Block Specific Countries (GeoIP): Restrict site access by country.
  • Block Specific Bots: Control which bots can access your site
  • CORS Headers: Enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing to allow trusted websites to access your site’s resources safely.
  • Hide PHP Version: Remove X-Powered-By header to hide PHP version information from headers.

Performance

  • Memory & Execution Limits: Raise your site’s memory and PHP execution time limits to stop “out of memory” and timeout errors.
  • Autosave Interval: Customize how often WordPress auto-saves your work.
  • Reliable Cron: Replace WP-Cron with a real server cron job, so scheduled tasks run on time instead of waiting on site traffic.
  • Disable Emojis: Stop loading emoji scripts and styles you don’t need.

Posts

  • Empty Trash Days: Set the number of days to keep deleted posts in trash.
  • Post Revisions: Limit or disable post revisions to save database space.
  • Disable Gutenberg Editor: Disable the block editor and revert to the classic editor.
  • Drag and Drop Ordering Posts: Rearrange posts via drag-and-drop.
  • Disable Comments: Disable comments site-wide with a single toggle.
  • Bulk Delete Posts: Delete posts in bulk from the admin panel.
  • Posts Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to posts for easy management of custom fields.

Taxonomies

  • Drag and Drop Ordering Taxonomies: Rearrange taxonomies via drag-and-drop.
  • Improved Taxonomy Meta Box: Enable lazy loading for taxonomy terms to improve performance.
  • Taxonomy Switcher: Switch taxonomy terms between taxonomies in a single click.
  • Taxonomy Term Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to taxonomy terms for easy management of custom fields.
  • Bulk Delete Terms: Delete taxonomy terms in bulk from the admin panel, with an optional filter for empty terms only or a name search, and an option to delete child terms along with their parent.

Users

  • Disable User Registration: Block all new user registrations.
  • Force Strong Passwords: Enforce password complexity rules (length, case, numbers, symbols).
  • Auto-Logout User: Auto-logout users after inactivity (customizable per role and time).
  • Hide Admin Bar: Hide the admin bar for specific users.
  • Redirect After Login/Logout: Customize where users go after logging in or out
  • Users Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to users for easy management of custom fields.
  • Last Login Tracking: Tracks when users log in, displays the information in the users table, and shows it on their profile pages.

Debug

  • WP Debug: Enable WordPress debug mode.
  • WP Debug Log: Log errors to a file.
  • WP Debug Display: Show/hide errors on the site.
  • Debug Log Viewer: View the debug log directly from the admin panel.
  • Maintenance Mode: Prevent all users from accessing the site but not the admin area.
  • Network Viewer: See every incoming request to your site in real time to spot suspicious activity and traffic spikes.
  • Email Log: Every email your site sends, logged with recipient, subject, and delivery status, so you can debug missing emails and SMTP problems.
  • Cron Viewer: See every scheduled task, find orphaned jobs left behind by deleted plugins, and run, pause, or resume any job on demand.

Media

  • Upload Max File Size: Set maximum upload file size.
  • Allow SVG Uploads: Enable SVG file uploads with security checks.
  • Allow Custom File Extension Uploads: Enable additional file types beyond WordPress defaults
  • Media Infinite Scrolling: Enable infinite scrolling for the media library.
  • Disable Big Image Threshold: Disable the threshold for displaying large images in the media library.

Plugins

  • Display Active Plugins First: Reorders the Plugins list to show active plugins at the top, separated from inactive plugins by a visual divider.
  • Enable Plugin Download: Adds a Download link to each plugin row, allowing admins to download any installed plugin as a .zip file directly from the admin panel. Requires PHP ZipArchive extension.

Important Disclaimer

This plugin modifies core WordPress functionality and behaviors. While we strive to maintain compatibility and stability:

  • The plugin’s features may work differently or not at all depending on your server configuration, hosting environment, and installed plugins
  • Some features may be restricted on certain hosting providers or server setups
  • We strongly recommend testing the plugin in a staging environment before using it on a production site
  • Always maintain regular backups of your website before making any changes

Server Compatibility Notice

Different server configurations may affect the plugin’s functionality:

  • Shared hosting environments might have restrictions that prevent certain features from working
  • Some features may require specific PHP extensions or server modules
  • Server-level email configurations might affect notification control features

Nginx and other servers that do not read .htaccess

Several features are normally delivered as .htaccess rules, which Apache and LiteSpeed (in Apache-compatibility mode) read, but Nginx, LiteSpeed in native mode, and IIS do not.

On those servers AdminEase automatically enforces the following in PHP instead, so they work the same way with nothing to configure:

  • Disable XML-RPC
  • Block Specific Countries
  • Block Specific Bots

The settings screen tells you which method is in use on your server. Features that change PHP or WordPress configuration rather than blocking requests (memory limit, upload size, file-editor lockdown, and similar) are unaffected either way.

The same applies to the backup copies AdminEase keeps of your wp-config.php and .htaccess files. They are stored in a folder with a long random name, which keeps them out of reach on every server, instead of relying on a rule file that only some servers read.

Block Specific Countries additionally need a geolocation source: either Cloudflare in front of your site or the GeoIP module on the server. If neither is available, the feature reports itself as unsupported rather than appearing to work.

If you experience any issues, please check with your hosting provider about server limitations.
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Log in to your WordPress admin panel
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New
  3. Search for “AdminEase”
  4. Click “Install Now” and then “Activate”
  5. Navigate to the AdminEase menu to configure your settings

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin zip file
  2. Log in to your WordPress admin panel
  3. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin
  4. Choose the downloaded zip file and click “Install Now”
  5. Activate the plugin
  6. Navigate to the AdminEase menu to configure your settings

After Activation

  1. Go to the AdminEase menu in your WordPress admin
  2. Explore the organized tabs (Updates, Security, Performance, etc.)
  3. Enable the features you need
  4. Save your settings

Important: We recommend testing on a staging site first and always maintain backups before making configuration changes.
sections.faq:
Why is my WordPress admin so slow, and how does AdminEase fix it?

The most common causes are a low PHP memory limit, a bloated database from unlimited post revisions, WP-Cron running on every admin page load, and a single poorly optimized plugin hammering admin-ajax.php. AdminEase fixes the first three directly from Performance and Posts settings (memory limit, post revision caps, disabling WP-Cron in favor of a real server cron), and its Network Viewer helps you spot the fourth by logging AJAX request volume by plugin path.

Do I need to know how to code to use AdminEase?

No coding knowledge is required. All features are accessible via an intuitive dashboard interface. Toggle features on or off with a click.

Will AdminEase slow down my site?

No, AdminEase is designed with performance in mind. It’s lightweight and you can enable only the features you need. Many features actually help improve your site’s performance.

Can I undo changes made by AdminEase?

Yes, you can toggle features on or off at any time. The plugin safely manages configuration changes and maintains backups of critical files.

Is AdminEase compatible with other plugins?

AdminEase is designed to work with most WordPress plugins and themes. However, since it modifies core WordPress behavior, conflicts may occasionally occur. We recommend testing on a staging site first.

The Password Protect Site form keeps reappearing after I enter the correct password. Why?

This almost always means a CDN or page cache (commonly Cloudflare with a “Cache Everything” rule) is serving a cached copy of the password page, so WordPress never sees that you logged in. AdminEase automatically adds a one-shot cache-busting parameter on login to work around this. For a fully reliable, leak-proof setup behind Cloudflare, also add a Cache Rule in the Cloudflare dashboard – When http.cookie contains "adminease_pps_auth_" Then Bypass cache – and purge the cache once. If only some pages are protected, make sure your “Cache Everything” rule respects origin cache headers or excludes the protected URLs.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

When you deactivate AdminEase, it safely restores your WordPress configuration to its previous state. All changes are reversed automatically.

Does AdminEase work on WordPress Multisite?

Basic compatibility is available, but some features may not work as expected on Multisite installations. Full Multisite support is planned for future releases.

Where can I get support?

For support, please visit our support page or contact us through the plugin’s support forum.

Support Resources:

  • Documentation
  • Tutorials
  • Support Forum
  • PrecisionWP Website
  • Adminease Pro

Unlock all Pro features with AdminEase Pro.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. AdminEase Pro is an add-on that runs alongside the free plugin, from the same dashboard. It needs the free plugin installed and active.

Security:

  • Block access by country using GeoIP with an allowlist for your own IP addresses and for search engine bots.
  • Disable XML-RPC with its own IP allowlist.
  • Disable the REST API with its own IP allowlist plus a list of REST routes that must keep working while the rest of the API stays blocked.

Posts and taxonomies:

  • Choose which post types the block editor is switched off for.
  • Which post types get drag-and-drop ordering.
  • Which taxonomies get drag-and-drop ordering.
  • Lazy loading for the taxonomy meta box for sites with a large number of terms.

Users:

  • Log users out after a period of inactivity, with the timeout set per role.

Settings and appearance:

  • Import discounts from a JSON file
  • A dark monospace “Terminal” theme for the free plugin’s Maintenance Mode page.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • Added: Send Email Through SMTP. Send your site’s emails through a real mailbox (Gmail, Microsoft 365, your host, or a service like Brevo or Mailgun) so password resets, order confirmations, and contact form messages reach the inbox instead of spam. Includes a test button to check your settings.
  • Added: Email Failure Alert. Get a notice in your admin area whenever your site fails to send an email, with a link to the details, so problems don’t go unnoticed.
  • Improved: The Email Log now shows the error message at the top of the details window, so you can see why an email failed right away.
  • Updated: Translation template.

2.1.2

  • Fixed: A security issue with where AdminEase stores its file backups. Before changing wp-config.php or .htaccess, AdminEase saves a copy of the original so you have something to fall back on. Those copies were kept in a folder inside your uploads folder with a fixed, predictable name, protected by rule files that Apache and IIS read but that Nginx and LiteSpeed in its own native mode ignore. On those servers the folder could be reached from the web by anyone who knew the address, which would expose the contents of your wp-config.php file, including your database details. The folder is now given a long random name that cannot be guessed, so it is protected on every server rather than only on some. Your existing backups are moved into the new folder for you the first time an admin page loads after updating, and there is nothing for you to do.
  • Improved: AdminEase’s design stylesheet was loading on every single admin page, including screens it has nothing to do with such as the post list, the media library, and other plugins’ settings pages. It is now loaded only where it is actually used: the AdminEase dashboard and the AdminEase metadata boxes on the post, term, and user edit screens. Every other admin page on your site now loads 62KB less CSS.
  • Improved: The AdminEase metadata boxes on the post, term, and user edit screens now use the standard WordPress admin font instead of downloading AdminEase’s own fonts, so those screens load faster and the boxes sit more naturally alongside the rest of the page. The AdminEase dashboard is unchanged.
  • Fixed: The media library’s preview background for SVG files and the loading notice shown while scrolling the media library were both missing their colors. They referenced design values that were never available on those screens, so the SVG preview had no backdrop, and the notice had no tint or border.

2.1.1

  • Fixed: Disable XML-RPC, Block Specific Countries, and Block Specific Bots did nothing on Nginx, IIS, and LiteSpeed running in its own native mode. These features worked by writing rules into the .htaccess file, which those servers never read, so the setting saved and reported success while your site stayed completely open. AdminEase now detects the server type and enforces all three in PHP instead, with the same result and nothing for you to configure. If you are on Apache or LiteSpeed in Apache-compatibility mode, nothing changes: the .htaccess rules are still used because blocking a request before it reaches PHP is faster.
  • Fixed: Moving a site between server types could leave a blocking rule behind in a file the new server does not read. Rules and stored settings are now cleaned up in both directions when you save.
  • Fixed: Country blocking could not be switched off again if the site lost its geolocation source, for example, when Cloudflare was removed or a host turned off its GeoIP module. The controls were greyed out in whatever state they were left in, so a block already switched on could not be undone, its country list was quietly dropped the next time any setting on the page was saved, and the rules already written to .htaccess were never removed. The controls now stay usable whatever the server supports, your country list is kept, and turning the feature off always clears the rules.
  • Improved: The Disable XML-RPC and Block Specific Countries settings now tell you when your server is being protected in PHP rather than through .htaccess, so it is clear the feature is active either way. Apache users see no extra text.
  • Fixed: On servers where the block is enforced in PHP, Block Specific Bots answered blocked bots without telling caches to keep the response out. A CDN or reverse proxy was free to store that refusal against the page and later serve it to real visitors, turning a bot block into an outage. The response is now marked uncacheable, matching Disable XML-RPC, Block Specific Countries, and Crawl Delay.
  • Updated: Translation template.

2.1.0

  • Added: Crawl Delay. A new Security feature that slows aggressive crawlers down instead of blocking them, so you keep the indexing but cap how fast bots can hit your server. It adds a Crawl-delay directive to the robots.txt WordPress generates (honored by Bingbot and YandexBot; Googlebot ignores it by design), and can optionally enforce the delay in PHP by answering bots that return too soon with 429 Too Many Requests and a Retry-After header. Each bot can be given its own delay, and logged-in users, admin pages, AJAX, WP-Cron, and WP-CLI are never throttled. If your site has a real robots.txt file, which replaces the one WordPress generates, the delays are written into it automatically inside a marked block; the rest of the file is left alone, a backup is taken first, and the block is removed again when you turn the feature off or deactivate the plugin. A robots.txt file is never created if you do not already have one. No .htaccess or wp-config.php changes are made, so it behaves the same on Apache, Nginx, and LiteSpeed.
  • Added: Bulk Delete Terms. A batched tool on the Taxonomies tab that permanently deletes taxonomy terms, with an optional “empty terms only” filter, a name search, and an option to delete child terms along with their parent. The taxonomy’s default term is always protected. Free covers Categories and Tags; Pro unlocks every registered taxonomy.
  • Added: A Stop button for Bulk Delete Posts and Bulk Delete Terms, so a long run can be ended safely.
  • Added: Turning on a tool such as Bulk Delete Posts now offers to save and activate it straight away, instead of leaving its buttons unresponsive until you save.
  • Fixed: A broad reliability pass over the admin tools. Progress bars now advance and finish with the right totals, batched runs no longer stall near the end, Taxonomy Switcher stops cleanly when something goes wrong, drag and drop ordering saves reliably, Cron Viewer times are correct, email previews open in an isolated frame, and errors always show a clear message instead of appearing to do nothing. With AdminEase Pro active, Bulk Delete Posts lists your custom post types again.
  • Fixed: Improved Taxonomy Meta Box could block Publish and Save Draft on post types with an empty hierarchical taxonomy, and could lose or duplicate selected terms or keep spinning after a search.
  • Fixed: The password-protected site login now only sends you back to pages on your own site.
  • Fixed: Max Execution Time refused to save when left empty. Clearing the field now simply removes the timeout AdminEase had set and hands the decision back to your server.
  • Fixed: Maintenance Mode’s page background and card no longer ignore your chosen colors, and the feature now supports a scheduled on/off window with a live countdown, an IP allowlist bypass, and two more page themes: Minimal and Split Screen. A fourth theme, Terminal, is available with AdminEase Pro.

short_description: Fix a slow WordPress admin, harden security, and control 60+ settings from one dashboard - no code required.
description:
AdminEase is an all-in-one WordPress admin toolkit that helps you manage updates, strengthen security, improve performance and streamline site maintenance without touching code. AdminEase makes everyday site management faster, safer, and easier from a clean, user friendly dashboard.

Is your WordPress admin slow? AdminEase fixes the most common causes and locks down security without touching code.

  • Fixes the slowdowns: Tackles low memory limits, database bloat, and WP-Cron overload, the most common causes of a sluggish admin.
  • Locks down security: Harden your site against common attacks with a click, nothing to configure.
  • One dashboard, 60+ settings: Toggle features on or off anytime, with nothing to break if you change your mind.

Key Benefits

  • No Coding Required: User-friendly interface for all skill levels
  • Enhanced Security: Protect your site from common vulnerabilities
  • Better Performance: Optimize WordPress for speed and efficiency
  • Complete Control: Toggle features on/off anytime without risk
  • Time Saver: Manage dozens of settings from one dashboard

Features

Updates and Notifications

  • Auto Update Core: Enable/disable automatic WordPress core updates.
  • Auto Update Plugins: Enable/disable automatic plugin updates.
  • Auto Update Themes: Enable/disable automatic theme updates.
  • Auto Update Translations: Enable/disable automatic translation updates.
  • Update Notification Emails: Receive emails when core, themes, or plugins are auto-updated.
  • New User Admin Notification Email: Notify admin on a new user registration.
  • User Password Change Admin Notification Email: Notify admin when a user changes their password.
  • Comment Admin Notification Email: Notify admin on new comments.
  • Send Email Through SMTP: Send your site’s email through a real mailbox instead of the web server, so password resets, order confirmations, and contact form messages reach the inbox instead of spam. Includes a test button that reports exactly what your mail server said.
  • Disable Admin Notices: Hide admin notices from plugins and themes.
  • Disable recovery mode email notification: Prevent WordPress from sending recovery mode emails.
  • Customize recovery mode recipient email: Set a custom email address to receive recovery mode notifications.

Security

  • Disable File Edit: Prevent editing theme/plugin files from the admin panel.
  • Disable File Mods: Prevent all file modifications in WordPress, including installing, updating, and deleting plugins and themes.
  • Disable XML-RPC: Block XML-RPC access to reduce attack surface, with an IP allowlist in AdminEase Pro.
  • Disable REST API: Block REST API access, with an IP allowlist in AdminEase Pro, plus the option to allow all HTTP requests to wordpress.org, including plugin/theme updates, version checks, and other API communications.
  • Disable Embeds: Stop automatic embedding of external content.
  • Hide WordPress Version: Remove version info from source code and feeds.
  • Password Protect Site: Protect your entire website with a password, featuring customizable themes, role-based bypasses, IP whitelisting, device remembering, and auto-disable scheduling.
  • Block Access to .htaccess/.htpasswd: Protect sensitive server files.
  • Disable Pingbacks: Prevent XML-RPC pingback abuse.
  • Block Author Scans: Prevent username enumeration.
  • Block Directory Browsing: Stop public directory listing.
  • Disable Script Concatenation (Admin): Prevent certain DoS attacks in admin.
  • Block Specific Countries (GeoIP): Restrict site access by country.
  • Block Specific Bots: Control which bots can access your site
  • CORS Headers: Enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing to allow trusted websites to access your site’s resources safely.
  • Hide PHP Version: Remove X-Powered-By header to hide PHP version information from headers.

Performance

  • Memory & Execution Limits: Raise your site’s memory and PHP execution time limits to stop “out of memory” and timeout errors.
  • Autosave Interval: Customize how often WordPress auto-saves your work.
  • Reliable Cron: Replace WP-Cron with a real server cron job, so scheduled tasks run on time instead of waiting on site traffic.
  • Disable Emojis: Stop loading emoji scripts and styles you don’t need.

Posts

  • Empty Trash Days: Set the number of days to keep deleted posts in trash.
  • Post Revisions: Limit or disable post revisions to save database space.
  • Disable Gutenberg Editor: Disable the block editor and revert to the classic editor.
  • Drag and Drop Ordering Posts: Rearrange posts via drag-and-drop.
  • Disable Comments: Disable comments site-wide with a single toggle.
  • Bulk Delete Posts: Delete posts in bulk from the admin panel.
  • Posts Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to posts for easy management of custom fields.

Taxonomies

  • Drag and Drop Ordering Taxonomies: Rearrange taxonomies via drag-and-drop.
  • Improved Taxonomy Meta Box: Enable lazy loading for taxonomy terms to improve performance.
  • Taxonomy Switcher: Switch taxonomy terms between taxonomies in a single click.
  • Taxonomy Term Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to taxonomy terms for easy management of custom fields.
  • Bulk Delete Terms: Delete taxonomy terms in bulk from the admin panel, with an optional filter for empty terms only or a name search, and an option to delete child terms along with their parent.

Users

  • Disable User Registration: Block all new user registrations.
  • Force Strong Passwords: Enforce password complexity rules (length, case, numbers, symbols).
  • Auto-Logout User: Auto-logout users after inactivity (customizable per role and time).
  • Hide Admin Bar: Hide the admin bar for specific users.
  • Redirect After Login/Logout: Customize where users go after logging in or out
  • Users Metadata Box: Adds a meta box to users for easy management of custom fields.
  • Last Login Tracking: Tracks when users log in, displays the information in the users table, and shows it on their profile pages.

Debug

  • WP Debug: Enable WordPress debug mode.
  • WP Debug Log: Log errors to a file.
  • WP Debug Display: Show/hide errors on the site.
  • Debug Log Viewer: View the debug log directly from the admin panel.
  • Maintenance Mode: Prevent all users from accessing the site but not the admin area.
  • Network Viewer: See every incoming request to your site in real time to spot suspicious activity and traffic spikes.
  • Email Log: Every email your site sends, logged with recipient, subject, and delivery status, so you can debug missing emails and SMTP problems.
  • Cron Viewer: See every scheduled task, find orphaned jobs left behind by deleted plugins, and run, pause, or resume any job on demand.

Media

  • Upload Max File Size: Set maximum upload file size.
  • Allow SVG Uploads: Enable SVG file uploads with security checks.
  • Allow Custom File Extension Uploads: Enable additional file types beyond WordPress defaults
  • Media Infinite Scrolling: Enable infinite scrolling for the media library.
  • Disable Big Image Threshold: Disable the threshold for displaying large images in the media library.

Plugins

  • Display Active Plugins First: Reorders the Plugins list to show active plugins at the top, separated from inactive plugins by a visual divider.
  • Enable Plugin Download: Adds a Download link to each plugin row, allowing admins to download any installed plugin as a .zip file directly from the admin panel. Requires PHP ZipArchive extension.

Important Disclaimer

This plugin modifies core WordPress functionality and behaviors. While we strive to maintain compatibility and stability:

  • The plugin’s features may work differently or not at all depending on your server configuration, hosting environment, and installed plugins
  • Some features may be restricted on certain hosting providers or server setups
  • We strongly recommend testing the plugin in a staging environment before using it on a production site
  • Always maintain regular backups of your website before making any changes

Server Compatibility Notice

Different server configurations may affect the plugin’s functionality:

  • Shared hosting environments might have restrictions that prevent certain features from working
  • Some features may require specific PHP extensions or server modules
  • Server-level email configurations might affect notification control features

Nginx and other servers that do not read .htaccess

Several features are normally delivered as .htaccess rules, which Apache and LiteSpeed (in Apache-compatibility mode) read, but Nginx, LiteSpeed in native mode, and IIS do not.

On those servers AdminEase automatically enforces the following in PHP instead, so they work the same way with nothing to configure:

  • Disable XML-RPC
  • Block Specific Countries
  • Block Specific Bots

The settings screen tells you which method is in use on your server. Features that change PHP or WordPress configuration rather than blocking requests (memory limit, upload size, file-editor lockdown, and similar) are unaffected either way.

The same applies to the backup copies AdminEase keeps of your wp-config.php and .htaccess files. They are stored in a folder with a long random name, which keeps them out of reach on every server, instead of relying on a rule file that only some servers read.

Block Specific Countries additionally need a geolocation source: either Cloudflare in front of your site or the GeoIP module on the server. If neither is available, the feature reports itself as unsupported rather than appearing to work.

If you experience any issues, please check with your hosting provider about server limitations.
